DECISION: should the new check stop a message outright, or only warn me about it?

Option A - stop the message
  What happens: when I write you something with a code in it that has no explanation, the message is refused and I have to rewrite it before it reaches you.
  Pros: you never read an unexplained code again, which is the whole point of the rule.
  Cons: if the check is ever wrong, it costs me a rewrite for nothing, and you wait slightly longer.
Option B - warn only
  What happens: the message reaches you either way, and I get a note afterwards saying what was wrong with it.
  Pros: nothing can ever get stuck.
  Cons: it is the same kind of thing as the rule that already failed twice, because it relies on me acting on the note.

My pick: A, because you chose an automatic check over a self-check for exactly this reason.
What would change my mind: if the check turns out to fire on messages that were actually fine.
